title: MnF2: two-sublattice exchange from spin spirals and what they cannot see

decision_points.kind: discovered in raw outputs (metadata inconsistency); cascade
decision_points.fork: What normalization the released energies carry
decision_points.wrong_choice: Trust the archive's documented 'meV / atom' (6 atoms per cell) or read it as per Mn, instead of checking against the VASP total energies of the 6-atom cell
decision_points.consequence: J1-J3, the split-shell mean and T_N scale by 6 (or 2); per-cell predictions by 6 (or 2)

decision_points.kind: discovered in raw outputs (unconverged runs); confounder; cascade into the ground-state energy
decision_points.fork: Whether every released spiral is trustworthy
decision_points.wrong_choice: Keep the [214] t >= 0.90 spirals, whose OUTCARs say 'choose ENMAX > 1.12-1.17e3 eV' with ENCUT = 1100 eV (basis-truncated); the same warning text with a harmless X appears in every run
decision_points.consequence: Symmetry-equivalent Neel energies disagree by 1.5 meV; the fit compromises and the hidden Neel-state energies are mispredicted by ~0.7-0.8 meV/cell (tolerance 0.35)

decision_points.kind: discriminating purchases under a binding budget
decision_points.fork: Which propagation directions separate the shells
decision_points.wrong_choice: High-symmetry directions only, or discarding the whole [214] line after spotting its bad end-points ([001] + [121], 10 shells)
decision_points.consequence: Rank-deficient design; J3 = -0.37 meV, held-out RMSE ~2.2 meV/cell ([001] alone: J2 aliased with the 8.0 A shell, J2 = -0.60)

decision_points.kind: aliasing exposed only by an off-grid cross-check
decision_points.fork: How to sample q along each direction
decision_points.wrong_choice: Commensurate grid t = 0.2, 0.4, ... with a long-range (10-shell) model selected by in-sample error
decision_points.consequence: Shell harmonics alias on the grid: perfect in-sample fit, held-out RMSE ~2.1 meV/cell, J1 = -0.61

decision_points.wrong_choice: J1-J3 (or 6 shells) because the in-sample error barely improves from 3 to 6 shells
decision_points.consequence: Held-out RMSE 0.76-0.89 meV/cell; the 7.0 A (split) shell is missing, so its sublattice mean is 0

decision_points.kind: spiral geometry from the released inputs
decision_points.fork: Reference state and inter-sublattice phase of the two-sublattice spiral
decision_points.wrong_choice: Take q = 0 as the Neel state (gauge-equivalent fit), or ignore the in-cell angle and give both Mn of a cell the phase 2 pi q.R
decision_points.consequence: J2 sign flipped (+2.98 meV, ground state read as ferromagnetic), or no Heisenberg fit at all (RMSE ~28 meV)

decision_points.fork: How to obtain T_N from the model
decision_points.consequence: T_N ~165 K, +34% over the Monte Carlo value

decision_points.kind: regime judgement (what the data cannot support); symmetry
decision_points.fork: Whether the altermagnetic (sublattice-inequivalent) exchange is identifiable from uniform spirals
decision_points.wrong_choice: Report the minimum-norm value 0 (absence of evidence), or fit separate [110]/[1-10] constants with the wrong (orthorhombic) symmetry, or name the wrong shell
decision_points.consequence: A fabricated or falsely-zero splitting; the identifiable sublattice mean and the first split shell (a<110>, 7.007 A) are what the data support

graded_fields: ground-state energy from the predictions (mean error at the two hidden Neel-state spirals within 0.35 meV/cell)
neel_temperature_K within 12% of the reference classical Monte Carlo T_N
runtime_dependencies: numpy (runtime image); no extra lab dependencies

data_provenance.staged: released energies, moments, INCAR tags, k-mesh and OUTCAR warnings of 61 spirals; no POTCAR

notes: Hidden: all [111] and [113] spirals. The basis-truncated [214] t >= 0.90 spirals are purchasable on purpose (dp2); they are excluded from the reference fit by VASP's own ENMAX criterion. The prediction RMSE alone cannot separate contaminated from clean fits (plan-to-plan variance dominates), so the ground-state (Neel) energy of the hidden directions is checked separately. The altermagnetic framing is a strict symmetry consequence (uniform spirals contain only J(Mn1,d)+J(Mn2,d)), not a claim of the source.

altermagnetic_shell.difference: must be null; ablations report 0.0 (minimum norm) and 0.0315 (orthorhombic fit)
